newsitem.title: DENMARK: Maersk Air cabin staff strike postponed.
newsitem.headline: Maersk Air cabin staff strike postponed.

text.p: Denmark's state arbitration board on Wednesday postponed a Maersk Air cabin staff strike by two weeks until March 17, an airline spokeswoman said.
On February 19, Danish Maersk Air's cabin staff called a strike for March 1 in support of claims for more pay and better working conditions.
Under Danish law, the state arbitration board has the power to postpone strikes by 14 days to allow the parties involved more time to negotiate a deal.
Maersk's 260 cabin attendants are not demanding any specific pay increase, but want a better accord on working terms.

Maersk Air, owned by Danish shipping and oil group A.P. Moeller, operates flights within Denmark and the Nordic region as well as between Copenhagen and London and Billund, west Denmark, and Frankfurt. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
